newsitem.title: BAHAMAS: Bahamas PM reappoints eight cabinet ministers.
newsitem.headline: Bahamas PM reappoints eight cabinet ministers.

text.p: Bahamas Prime Minister Hubert Ingraham, whose Free National Movement won a landslide reelection last Friday, has reappointed eight cabinet ministers.

Ingraham was sworn in on Tuesday night at Government House for a second term and named Deputy Prime Minister Frank Watson minister of national security with responsibility for public service and public utilities.
William Allen retained the post of minister of finance and planning.
Former Transportation Minister Tennyson Wells was named attorney general and minister of justice, and C.A. Smith, former minister of public safety and immigration, was appointed minister of tourism.
Janet Bostwick was reappointed minister of foreign affairs and Ivy Dumont retained the education portfolio.
Theresa Moxey-Ingraham, who was minister of health in the last government, was named minister of Labour, Immigration and Training.
Algernon Allen, former minister of youth and culture, became minister of housing and social development. Further announcements were expected late Wednesday.

Ingraham, whose Free National Movement won 34 of 40 house seats and 57 percent of the popular vote in Friday's election, pledged on Tuesday to continue policies of accountability and prudent management.

"We pledge that, as in our first term, transparency, accountability and integrity in public affairs, judicious management of our nation's finances and natural resources, and economic and social justice will be our code of conduct," Ingraham told thousands of people at the swearing-in ceremony.
He promised that the FNM would intensify efforts to train young people so that they would be "beneficiaries of an education system that is second to none."
Former Prime Minister Sir Lynden Pindling, who was unseated by Ingraham five years ago, announced his intention to resign as leader of the Progressive Liberal Party after 32 years in that position.
Pindling, who retained his South Andros seat in the election, did not give a date for his resignation and said a transition team was being put in place.
